title: Runtime Is the New Security Frontier
author: Eliot Ferstl
excerpt: Prevention and perimeter tools stop known threats at the door. The harder problem lives at runtime, after workloads start doing real work.

title: Building Defense That Assumes Compromise
author: Eliot Ferstl
excerpt: Designing for a world where compromise is assumed changes what you build — it means planning for the moment defenses are already inside the perimeter.

title: 0.005% of What?
author: Eliot Ferstl
excerpt: Most published false positive rates in runtime security can't be verified by the reader. Here's how the same soak data produced two very different honest numbers.

title: Three Silent Failures Between You and Sidecar Injection
author: Eliot Ferstl
excerpt: 'kubectl label deployment' writes to the Deployment object's metadata, not to 'spec.template.metadata.labels', where pods actually get their labels. If your sidecar injection is label-selected, the command reports success and nothing happens. Here's why, and the fix.

title: Why We Ship Our Security Webhook Fail-Open
author: Eliot Ferstl
excerpt: Anything that installs an admission webhook puts itself in the critical path of pod creation. One field, 'failurePolicy', decides whether the vendor's outage becomes yours. The textbook answer is fail-closed. We ship the opposite, on purpose.

title: The Rules We Use To Define False Positives
author: Eliot Ferstl
excerpt: Our largest false positive soak to date is still running: 94 pods, 14 namespaces, 7 days, 0 attacks. Before the results are published, here's exactly how they'll be scored: the definitions, thresholds, and denominators we can't quietly adjust after seeing the data.
